A substantive refutation uses delta=0,r=1/4,A=1/2 and any fixed 0<alpha<1. For every n>=2 and every beta there are all-complier constant-additive-effect populations with n1=floor(n/2), so all inner LATE classes are nonempty. The fourth-moment inequality forces both centered W arrays to vanish, their means agree at LATE, and every assignment has statistic and critical value zero. Thus every admitted model has coverage 1 and the nested infimum is 1, not 1-alpha. scratch/Check.lean also compiles an explicit Theta instance at n=4 with these constants. No empty-infimum or r=1/2 parity artifact is needed.

Use k=1,delta=0,e=1/4,A=4,B=1/2,r=1/4 and any fixed 0<alpha<1. For every n>=4 and every beta, take n1=floor(n/2), centered distinct covariates x_i=(2*i-n+1)/n, all compliers, y_i(0)=0,y_i(1)=beta. Then mean(x^2)=(n^2-1)/(3*n^2)>=1/4 and mean(x^4)<=1<=4, so Xi is nonempty, with both residual arrays zero. In every Xi model with B=1/2, the residual fourth-moment bound forces both residual arrays to be zero. On full-rank assignments the adjusted statistic at LATE is zero. The centered second-moment lower bound, fourth-moment upper bound and arm balance give a uniform O(1/n) bound on the probability of either singular arm, by Chebyshev applied to the arm means of x and x^2. Hence every admitted coverage is at least 1-O(1/n), the nested infimum tends to 1, and the printed universal nominal equality fails for nonempty classes. This argument accommodates the chosen deterministic rule on singular arms.
